MCF update (11-23): wild Monday, still green

Quick heads-up first: I'm done with daily and weekly summaries. They got too daunting. From now on I'll just post when I can. New here? See previous posts for the basics.

Today in short (image 3):

  • The S&P was up about 5%, the Nasdaq about 7% and Nvidia about 31%. Huge day.
  • Primary still finished green: +0.5R / +$185.
  • That's 2 green days in a row, after last week's first-ever green week (+4.1R / +$756). Now going for two green weeks back to back.

How the system handled the chaos:

  • Peaked at +5.4R around lunch, closed at +0.5R.
  • Our gap-down shorts fought the rally all afternoon.
  • ETF dip buys went 6 for 6.
  • An automatic stop shut off two losing setups.
  • All 10 accounts closed clean, no glitches.
  • The new "burst brake" blocked about 290 runaway trades in the testing accounts.

Today's standouts (image 1):

Two machine-made setups had great days and are also up overall. The image walks through each one step by step:

  • Late-Morning Pop Fade: when the market's down late morning, short a weak stock that suddenly pops. +11R today, +25R total over 9 days.
  • Late Quiet-Day Short: shorts sleepy stocks between 2 and 3 PM when the Nasdaq dips. +5R today, +32R total over 11 days.

Both are young, so promising, not proven. And to be clear, this is paper trading, not advice.

Top 10 with tougher stats (image 2):

New columns this time:

  • Without its best day: is it more than one lucky day?
  • Last 10 days: is it still working?
  • Worst day: how bad does a bad day get?

The ones I trust most stay green on all of them, like Gap-Down Recovery Fade (Primary).

Quick facts:

  • 10 practice accounts, all paper money (Alpaca).
  • A "setup" is one rule for when to get in and out of a trade.
  • R = what you risked. +1R means you made what you risked.
  • Every number is after trading costs.
  • Primary is the main account and the real scoreboard. Everything else is testing.
  • Setups move up or down based on results. Weak ones go to the Graveyard, which never deletes anything.
  • Big losing days are handled by automatic rules, not by me jumping in.
  • We've screened about 27,000 ideas to get to 4 setups in Primary.

Thanks as always!

Educational only — not financial advice.
